headline: Bohm's slam sparks comeback as Phillies beat Twins 7-5
recap: The Phillies trailed 5-0 at Target Field on Sunday after Brooks Lee's first-inning grand slam and a Kody Clemens solo homer in the third off Andrew Painter, but rallied to beat the Twins 7-5. Alec Bohm's own grand slam highlighted a four-run sixth that pulled Minnesota starter Dean Kremer from the game, and Philadelphia went ahead for good in the eighth on a two-run single from Bryan De La Cruz and an RBI double from Luis Arraez off Andrew Morris (L, BS). Painter was charged with all five Twins runs over five innings, Orion Kerkering (W, 7-1) worked a scoreless seventh, and Jhoan Duran struck out three in the ninth for his 26th save.
Philadelphia is 67-58, second in the NL East, 7.5 games behind the first-place Braves, and has won three straight.

The Phillies open a series with the Miami Marlins Monday at Citizens Bank Park, with Cristopher Sanchez set to start opposite Miami's Janson Junk. First pitch is 6:40 PM ET. DraftKings lists the Phillies as -246 favorites on the moneyline.
